S. zoaE This has reference to your letter dated May 5, 2025, requesting for the Department's guidance on how to proceed on the non-cooperation of parties in barangay proceedings leaving barangay cases unresolved. Per your representation, you are currently handling a complaint at the barangay level. The issue is the respondent refused to appear before the lupon. You made every reasonable effort to mediate and facilitate resolution yet those efforts were unsuccessful. Given that the complainant is a family member, she has now opted to discontinue the complaint against the respondent, and instead, expressed a desire to avoid any further conflict. You find yourself in a challenging situation, as the case remains technically unresolved and there appears no definitive procedural steps to formally conclude or escalate it. This ambiguity may cast your Lupon in a potentially unfavorable position during the the evaluations for the Lupong Tagapamayapa Incentives Awards (L TIA). Further, you express apprehension regarding the potential recurrence of analogous cases in the future, which may imply a, lack of proactive measures on your part. In light of this, you now seek guidance and/or recommendation of the following courses of action, to wit: 1. How should barangays officially document or close a case where neither party seeks further proceedings nor resolution, especially when one party refuses barangay jurisdictiön; 2. What legal remedies or procedural safeguards are available to barangays to protect themselves from criticisms of inaction during evaluations and audits such as L TIA; 3. Could the DILG issue a uniform guideline or advisory for barangays in handling cases that involve contested jurisdiction or accusations involving family members, especially where mental health concerns are raised; and 4. What is the appropriate handling of written responses like that submitted by Mr. Alfredo Diano Jr. which contain extensive legal citations and arguments, but no willingness to participate in barangay dispute mechanisms. The Katarungang Pambarangay Law, was established as a community-based system of dispute resolution wherein it authorizes the barangay to emediate and conciliate disputes among its residents through the Punong Barangay and the Lupong "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Tagapamayapa. This system encourages the resolution of conflicts outside of formal court proceedings, especially those involving personal, property, or neighborhood Issues. In Section 515 of the Local Government Code of 1991, provides the following instances in case of refusal or failure of any parties or witnesses to appear before the lupon or pangkat Section 515. Refusal or Failure of Any Pany or Wltness to Appear before the Lupon or Pangkat. - Refusal or willful failure of any patty or witness to appear before the lupon or pangkat in compliance with a summons issued pursuant to the provisions on the Katarungang Pambarangay under Chapter 7, Title Ill of this Code may be punished by the city or municipal COUN as for indirect contempt of court upon application filed therewith by the lupon chairman, the pangkat chairman, Or by any of the contending parties. Such refusal or willful failure to appear shall be reflected in the records of the lupon secretary or in the minutes of the pangkat secretaty and shall bar the complainant who fails to appear, from seeking judicial recourse for the same cause of action, and the respondent who refuses to appear, from filing any counterclaim arising out of, or necessarily connected with the complaint. Further, the implementing rules and regulations of the Katarungang Pambarangay provides for the procedures and the corresponding sanctions on the parties' failure to appear — Section 8. Failure to appear— a. Sanctions The complaint may be dismissed when complainant, after due notice, refuses or willfully fails to appear without justifiable reason on the date set for mediation, conciliation or arbitration. Such dismissal order by the Punong Barangay/Pangkat Chairman after giving the complainant an opportunity to explain his non-appearance shall be cehified to by the Lupon or Pangkat Secretary as the case may be, and shall bar the complainant from seeking judicial recourse for the same cause of action as that dismissed. Upon a similar failure of the respondent to appear, any counterclaim he has made that arises from or is necessarily connected with complainant's action, may be dismissed Such dismissal, ordered by the Punong Barangay/Pangkat Chairman after giving the respondent an opportunity to explain his non-appearance shall be certified to by the Lupon or Pangkat Secretary, as the case may be, and shall bar the respondent from filing such counterclaim in court or any govemment office for adjudication. xxx a. xxx Procedure xxx Page 2 of 3

1.1 In case a party fails to appear for mediation, the Punong Barangay shall set a date for the absent party/ies to appear before him to explain the reason for hisftheir failure to appear at the hearing; 1.2 If the Punong Barangay finds after hearing that the failure or refusal of the complaint to appear is without justifiable reason, he shall [1] dismiss the complaint; [2] direct the issuance of and attest to the certification to bar the filing of the action in court or any govemment office; and [31 apply with the local trial court for punishment of the recalcitrant party as for indirect contempt of court; and 1.3 In case of similar willful failure or refusal of the respondent to appear for mediation before the Punong Barangay, the latter shall: [11 dismiss the respondent's counterclaim; [2] direct the issuance of and attest to the certification to bar the filing of the action in court or any govemment office; and [3] apply with the local trial court for punishmeht of the recalcitrant patty as for indirect contempt of court; and Clearly therefore, the failure of the complainant to appear without justifiable cause such as lack of interest to pursue the case, will cause the dismissal of his/her complaint and may be barred from filing a case in court. On one hand, in case of refusal or willful failure of the respondent to appear in obedience to the summons, the latter may be barred from filing any counterclaim arising from the complaint. In all cases where the respondent fails to appear at the mediation proceedings before the Punong Barangay, and his/her refusal is without justifiable cause after notice and hearing, the same shall be sufficient basis for the issuance of a Certification to File Action (CFA). In a similar vein, should the complainant fail or refuses to appear therein, a corresponding Certification to Bar Action (CBA) will be duly issued. With regard your other concerns such as the issuance of uniform guidelines, we regret to inform you that it is beyond the province of this level to immediately address the same as it is a policy formulation matter. Nevertheless, we assure you that we will take due consideration of this request for uniform guidelines or advisory for barangays in handling similar cases, the Office of the Undersecretary for Local Government is herein copy furnished for this purpose. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have provided you sufficient guidance on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P.
